title: Raspberry Lemon Burst Cupcakes
shortDescription: Tart raspberry puree meets fresh lemon zest in a soft cupcake, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes mix real raspberry puree into the batter, not just the frosting. Fresh lemon zest cuts through the sweetness so every bite feels bright, not heavy. I tested this recipe three times in my home kitchen to get the fruit to sugar ratio right. Too much puree made the batter runny, so I learned to reduce it slightly on the stove first. The frosting uses fresh lemon juice and a swirl of raspberry sauce for a two tone look. It pipes up tall and holds its shape well at room temperature. This is a great pick for spring brunches or anytime you want a classic cupcake with a fruity twist.
ingredients: 1/3 cup raspberry puree, seeds strained out
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
3 tbsp raspberry puree, for frosting swirl
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla and lemon zest.
Alternate adding the flour mix and milk, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until combined.
Gently fold in 1/3 cup raspberry puree. Do not overmix or the color will streak too much.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
For frosting, beat 1 cup butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in lemon juice until frosting is light and spreadable. Swirl in raspberry puree by hand for a marbled look.
Pipe frosting onto fully cooled cupcakes. Top with a small dab of raspberry puree or fresh lemon zest.
tips: Strain your raspberry puree through a fine mesh sieve to remove seeds. This keeps the batter and frosting smooth.
Reduce the raspberry puree in a small pan over low heat for 5 minutes if it looks watery. Let it cool before using.
Zest your lemon before you juice it. It is much easier to zest a whole lemon than a squeezed one.
Chill the frosting for 10 minutes if it feels too soft to pipe in a warm kitchen.

faq.question: Can I use frozen raspberries instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Yes, thaw them fully and drain extra liquid before blending. Frozen raspberries work well since they get pureed anyway.

faq.question: Why did my batter turn out pink and streaky?
faq.answer: That happens if you overmix after adding the raspberry puree. Fold it in gently with just a few strokes.

faq.question: Can I make this recipe dairy free?
faq.answer: Swap the butter for a plant based baking stick and use oat milk. The texture stays close to the original.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Bring to room temperature before serving for the best texture.

conclusion: These Raspberry Lemon Burst Cupcakes bring a tart sweet balance that feels fresh, not fussy. Once you get the puree ratio right, this recipe becomes a easy go to for spring baking.
